correctness.rationale: The quotient V and socle layer are residue-field modules without a coefficient-field assumption. Nondegeneracy makes any proper ideal containing a nonzero vector modulo m² also contain m² (multiply by a partner giving a nonzero socle element); the only other proper ideals are 0 and m² itself. Thus the proper nonzero ideals are exactly the J_U including J_{0 subspace}=m². For a d-space U, its perfect-pairing annihilator has dimension r−d, so precisely T_{r−d} partners W give zero; this applies even in characteristic two, and counts ordered pairs including equality. For any k, count zero-free tuples with zero, one or two proper factors; three proper factors vanish. The two-proper nonzero outcomes are all m², giving the stated distribution and total complement, also at k=1. For fixed r, deg T_r=⌊r²/4⌋, and deg C_r≤max_t(rt−3t²/4)≤r²/3<2⌊r²/4⌋. Consequently the pair zero probability tends to zero and for fixed k≥3 the complement is O(T_r^(2−k)). Rank two gives T₂=q+3, C₂=3q+6 and the displayed probability. An initially suspected rank-three discrepancy is resolved: T₁(2)=2, not 3, so C₃(2)=16+7·5+7·2+1=66, and the frozen counts (18 ideals, 101 zero pairs, 5213 zero triples) are correct. Separate exhaustive generation by repeatedly adjoining one element and taking ideal closure reproduced these counts; in the characteristic-four example with additive group Z/4⊕(F₂)², x²=y²=2 and xy=2x=2y=0, the same check gave 7 ideals, 25 zero pairs and 288 zero triples. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The two exhaustive reproductions are finite checks only. Scope in general residue fields and in mixed characteristic follows from the proof; the threshold fixes r and k.

value.rationale: The ideal-product distribution is a motivated exact invariant from an existing non-chain universality question. This class is rich enough to vary the field size, form and ring characteristic, and the result identifies which of those data the invariant retains. The large-field transition sharply separates two from three factors even though the Loewy length stays fixed. Both the exact law and the contrasting limit are useful for assessing which universality claims from chains extend to other local rings.
residual_risks: No law is claimed for degenerate pairings, higher-dimensional socles, or growing r or k. Independence concerns ring data beyond the fixed q,r, not independence of residue-field order.
